# Form

A form that validates with the browser's own constraints (`required`, `type="email"`, `pattern`) and shows server errors on the matching fields. Pass `errors` straight from your action; each message lands on the field with that `name`, and focus moves to the first field with an error. Bind an accepted action answer with the framework-free `formErrors` constructor in `@/lib/ouro/form-answer`. Server errors only show: unlike the browser's checks they never block the next submit, so the user can always send the form again. A Form submits only itself: its submit event stops there, so a Form in a sheet inside another Form never submits the outer one. It renders a `<form>`, so `action` and `method` pass through; to submit through React Router, render its `Form`: `render={<RouterForm />}`.

```tsx
import { Form } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/form/form";
```

## Example

```tsx
// Checked in the browser, with no router or server: each submit's own answer, so the same mistake shows again.
import { formErrors } from "@/lib/ouro/form-answer";
const [answer, setAnswer] = useState<{ errors: FormErrors }>();
<Form
  errors={formErrors(answer, answer?.errors)}
  onSubmit={(event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const name = String(new FormData(event.currentTarget).get("name"));
    setAnswer({ errors: name === "admin" ? { name: "That name is taken." } : {} });
  }}
>
  <TextField label="Display name" name="name" required />
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</Form>
// With a router: the action's answer.
import { formErrors } from "@/lib/ouro/form-answer";
const actionData = useActionData<typeof action>();
<Form method="post" errors={formErrors(actionData, actionData?.errors)} render={<RouterForm />}>
  <TextField label="Email" name="email" type="email" required />
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</Form>
// The action answers { errors: { general, email } }: map its keys to this form's field names.
const errors = actionData?.errors;
<Form method="post" errors={formErrors(actionData, { form: errors?.general, email: errors?.email })} render={<RouterForm />}>
  <TextField label="Email" name="email" type="email" required />
  <Button type="submit">Subscribe</Button>
</Form>
```

## Usage

A submit is checked in this order. First the browser's own checks (`required`, `type="email"`, `pattern`): a failure stops the submit, marks each failing field with the browser's message and moves focus to the first. Then your `onSubmit`, which runs only when those pass and can still call `event.preventDefault()`. Then the server, whose answer comes back as `errors`.

The keys of `errors` are your fields' `name`s, and `form` is the message about the whole form. An action that answers with other keys is mapped where you pass them: `errors={formErrors(data, { form: data?.errors?.general, email: data?.errors?.email })}`. A key that no field in this form is named shows at the top of the form and warns in development with the key, this form's field names and the fix; with two forms on one route, pass each only its own keys.

Why `formErrors(answer, messages)`: Form has to tell a new answer from the same one rendered again. `answer` is the object your action or submit handler gave back for this submit, and `messages` are its errors by field name. Each new `answer` object is a new answer, even with the same messages: every message shows again, including one the user cleared, and focus moves once. Rendering again with the same `answer` is not: a message the user cleared by editing its field stays cleared, and focus stays put. So build the value in the render, as the examples do. Form never guesses that an answer arrived from a submit starting, a wait or a navigation. You choose which answer belongs to this form, so with two Forms on one route, pass each its own. When the answer is the same object every time (a cache) or not an object at all, add a key you change when a new answer comes in: `formErrors(data, data.errors, { key: savedAt })`.

A plain object, `errors={{ email: "Taken." }}`, still works, but Form compares it by its content: the same mistake made twice looks like no change, so it does not show again. Use `formErrors` for answers, from the first render, while the answer is still `undefined`: switching between a plain object and `formErrors` is not a new answer, so it moves no focus and keeps what the user cleared. The answer lives in memory only: JSON, a spread, structured cloning and passing it from a server component keep the messages and lose the answer. Reconstruct beside Form in each environment, from the answer or key you have there; the value never keeps or serializes the rest of the answer.

The message about the whole form is an alert (`role="alert"`). It is in the page only while there is a message, and each answer adds a new one with its text already in it, which is what screen readers announce; `getByRole("alert")` finds nothing on a form without one. A field's message is not an alert: it is that control's description, so assert it with `toHaveAccessibleDescription`.

After a submit that leaves field errors, focus moves to the first field, and once the browser has painted that move the alert opens with a visually hidden summary, such as "Couldn't save: 1 problem. Name: You already have a recipe called Pasta.". Screen readers announce the summary after the field, so they speak the field, then its error. The same summary is not announced again while the errors stand, and a changed error, or one the user fixed and got back, announces again. Pass `errorSummary` to translate it. A message at the top of the form counts as one problem.

Focus moves to the first field with an error when errors arrive after a submit. A page that loads with `errors` already set (a post without JavaScript, or a reload) shows them in the server HTML and moves no focus: nothing was submitted from this page, and taking focus on load would drop a keyboard or screen-reader user into the middle of a page they have not read. To send them to the errors on load, put an in-page link to the form in your page's own error summary.

## Use instead when

- Use `EditSheet` instead for a form in a dialog that saves and closes, and a plain `<form>` when nothing needs validating.

## Props

Type: `FormProps`.

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` | The fields and the submit button. |
| `className` | `string` | Layout only: margins, width, grid placement. Fields stack with a gap by default; appearance classes warn in development. |
| `errors` | `ReadonlyFormErrors \| FormErrorValue \| null` | Errors by field name, from your action or submit handler: `errors={formErrors(actionData, actionData?.errors)}` (import `formErrors` from `@/lib/ouro/form-answer`). Each changed answer, including an equal one, shows its messages again and moves focus once. Rebuilding the value or its mapped messages with the same answer is not a new answer: nothing moves. Each one shows on the field with that `name`, which gets `aria-invalid` and links the message, in the server HTML too. A field's own `error` prop wins over it, and a message goes away once the user changes that field. When new errors arrive, focus moves to the first field with one, in page order. The `form` key shows in an alert at the top of the form, in the server HTML too; a key no rendered field is named joins it once the page hydrates, and warns in development. A message is text or a React node (a message with a link), and an array is several messages. With the same answer, a message the user cleared stays cleared, even if its key goes away and comes back; messages the user hasn't cleared update in place (new text, a new React node), without moving focus or replacing the alert, though a screen reader may read changed alert text. No answer (`null`/`undefined`) is not a new answer either, and keeps what the user cleared. Cached/reused or primitive answers need `{ key }`, changed only when a new answer comes in, never when a submit starts: `formErrors(data, data.errors, { key: savedAt })`. Form doesn't work out which of a router's data belongs to this form: pass this form's own. A plain object (`errors={{ email: "Taken." }}`) works for errors you show yourself, compared by content, so the same mistake twice doesn't show again; use `formErrors` for answers, from the first render: switching between the two is not a new answer, and keeps what the user cleared. JSON, a spread, structured cloning or a server component's props keep only the messages: build the value beside Form, on the server and in the browser. These errors only show: they never block the next submit, so the user can always send the form again (a server error may be fixed by changing another field, or by trying again). The browser's own checks (`required`, `type="email"`) still block a submit. |
| `errorSummary` | `FormErrorSummary` | Translates the summary a screen reader hears first after a submit that leaves field errors: how many problems there are, and the first in page order, which is the field focus moves to. `label` is that field's label text, or `undefined` when it cannot be read; `message` is its error, or `""` when that cannot be read. A message at the top of the form counts as one problem. The summary is visually hidden: each field shows its own error. |

## Native attributes

Also accepts the attributes in React's `FormHTMLAttributes` and `HTMLAttributes` (`id`, `aria-*`, event handlers), passed to the rendered element, except those named on this page.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `result`: Not a prop. Bind the accepted answer inside `errors`: `errors={formErrors(answer, messages)}`.
- `validationErrors`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `errors`: `<Form errors={actionData?.errors}>`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`).

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `ErrorMessage`

One error message: text, or a React element for a message that carries a link or other markup.

```ts
type ErrorMessage = string | ReactElement;
```

### `FormErrorSummary`

What a `FormProps.errorSummary` receives: the number of problems, and the first one in page order.

```ts
type FormErrorSummary = (
  count: number,
  first: {
    label: string | undefined;
    message: string;
  },
) => string;
```

### `FormErrorValue`

A read-only message snapshot with private, in-memory answer identity. Create it with `formErrors`; JSON, spread, structured cloning and server-component transport retain only the messages, not its identity. Reconstruct it beside Form on the server and in the browser. Array containers are snapshotted and frozen; React elements are retained, not cloned. React nodes are render inputs, not a promise that arbitrary node graphs JSON-serialize. Snapshot arrays are readonly, so use this type or `ReadonlyFormErrors`, not a mutable `FormErrors` annotation. This is not deep immutability of React nodes. TypeScript's `Array.isArray` narrows to `any[]` and can bypass readonly; runtime freezing still rejects mutation.

```ts
type FormErrorValue = ReadonlyFormErrors & { readonly [errorValueBrand]: true };
```

### `ReadonlyErrorMessages`

A read-only message view accepted by fields and Form; mutable input arrays remain valid.

```ts
type ReadonlyErrorMessages = ErrorMessage | readonly ErrorMessage[];
```

### `ReadonlyFormErrors`

A read-only display projection for Form and EditSheet; mutable raw `FormErrors` remain valid inputs.

```ts
type ReadonlyFormErrors = Readonly<Record<string, ReadonlyErrorMessages | null | undefined>>;
```
